frequency_question: How often does a country successfully establish domestic production of complex foreign missiles within a two-year timeframe of urgent wartime need?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states attempting to localize production of advanced foreign-designed missiles (cruise, anti-ship, or air-to-air) during an active high-intensity conflict. Excludes peacetime transfers of technology or simple unguided munitions (artillery, basic rockets).
window: 24 months from initiative start to operational facility

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng III production expansion
Iran domestic anti-ship missile lines from Chinese blueprints
Pakistan Anza missile domestic assembly transition

coverage_note: 5 named historical analogues; historical data for wartime transfer and rapid domestic missile manufacturing setup is sparse but bounded.
known_gaps: Modern cruise missile complexity involves supply chains far more intricate than 1980s or 1990s analogues, potentially lowering modern success rates.
validity_reason: Industrial base resilience and supply chain globalization structures remain stable across this decade.
